ai.description: Darwin’s Large Fan-throated Lizard reaches 8–9 cm. It is brown with dark dorsal blotches and a distinct white lateral stripe. Males display a large, vibrant blue and black throat fan during mating.
ai.identificationRemarks: Distinguish *Sarada darwini* by its unique, vibrant blue-and-black throat fan (dewlap) that lacks the distinct white or yellow margins found in other fan-throated species.
ai.habitat: *Sarada darwini* inhabits the rocky, open plateaus and scrublands of the northern Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: During the breeding season, males perform conspicuous displays by rapidly extending a vibrant, fan-like throat pouch to attract mates and intimidate rival males.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Sarada darwini* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–8 eggs. Breeding occurs annually during the monsoon season, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: Sarada darwini is endemic to the Deccan Plateau in India, primarily inhabiting the states of Maharashtra and Karnataka at elevations between 400 and 900 meters.
